comparison: Both strongly support the chlorophyllous embryo phenotype in osnf-yb7 mutants (C1, C38-C43). OpenEval emphasizes the multi-method experimental validation (TEM, chlorophyll measurements, confocal microscopy), while peer reviewers explicitly affirmed this as the core finding with 'convincing evidence.' OpenEval includes C45 (light dependency) which peer review addresses separately in R10.

Both strongly support direct transcriptional regulation by OsNF-YB7 of chlorophyll biosynthesis genes (C3, C54-C55, C57, C59-C61). OpenEval details the convergence of ChIP-qPCR, EMSA, and DLR assays. Peer reviewers praised the 'multi-layered experimental validation' and 'rigorous experimental approach' with no concerns raised.

Both support OsNF-YB7's repression of OsGLK1 (C62-C66, C69-C70, C120-C121). OpenEval notes the failed EMSA (C67) as a mechanistic gap requiring cofactors, while peer reviewers accepted the ChIP-qPCR and DLR data without questioning the negative EMSA result, treating it as consistent with NF-Y complex biology.

Both strongly support the protein-protein interaction between OsNF-YB7 and OsGLK1 (C4, C90-C98). OpenEval emphasizes convergence across Y2H, BiFC, Co-IP, and split-LUC assays. Peer reviewers explicitly praised these approaches, with Reviewer 3 noting the interaction data and Reviewer 1 mentioning 'protein interaction combine for convincing evidence.'

Perfect agreement on OsGLK1 overexpression phenotype (C71-C73, C118). Both treat the gain-of-function genetic evidence as strong support for OsGLK1's role in chlorophyll biosynthesis. OpenEval notes phenotypic similarity to osnf-yb7, while peer reviewers accepted this as confirmatory evidence without critique.

Both support genetic epistasis analysis in higher-order mutants (C74-C75, C119, C143). OpenEval emphasizes partial suppression in triple mutants and persistence of other embryo defects demonstrating specificity. Peer reviewers accepted this genetic separation of functions as part of comprehensive experimental design without questions.

Both support RNA-seq data showing upregulation of chlorophyll biosynthesis genes (C49-C52). OpenEval also includes antagonistic regulation analysis (C76-C80) which peer review addresses in R7. Peer reviewers accepted transcriptomic data as robust, with Reviewer 3 noting gene expression analysis and Reviewer 1 mentioning gene expression profiles as convincing evidence.

Perfect agreement on overlapping DNA binding sites (C81-C89). Both accept ChIP-qPCR, EMSA, ChIP-seq reanalysis, and motif analysis as demonstrating OsNF-YB7 and OsGLK1 recognize similar sequences. Peer reviewers treated this as part of comprehensive molecular characterization without concerns.

Both support the multi-layered regulatory model (C6-C8, C37, C131). OpenEval synthesizes three mechanisms: direct repression, OsGLK1 transcriptional repression, and protein-protein interaction. Peer reviewers explicitly affirmed the dual mechanism, with Reviewer 3 noting 'broad involvement' and Reviewer 1 emphasizing insights into negative regulation.

Perfect agreement on light dependency experiments (C45, C47-C48, C111-C112). Both support the conclusion that intrinsic signals repress chlorophyll biosynthesis. OpenEval details dark treatment and hull removal experiments, while peer reviewers accepted this as supporting evidence for genetic basis without questions.

Both address negative EMSA results (C67-C68, C122-C124). OpenEval rates this as UNCERTAIN, noting the mechanistic gap about required cofactors. Peer reviewers SUPPORTED the interpretation, accepting the explanation that NF-Y proteins function as heterotrimeric complexes without critique of the failed in vitro binding.

Both support broader regulatory scope of OsNF-YB7 compared to OsGLKs (C144-C147). OpenEval cites genetic analysis and ChIP-seq/RNA-seq comparisons. Peer reviewers accepted this comparative genomic analysis as consistent with genetic data showing OsNF-YB7 affects multiple developmental aspects while OsGLKs are chlorophyll-specific.

Both support antagonistic regulation of shared targets (C76-C80). OpenEval emphasizes RNA-seq showing 60.6% genes activated in both mutants and 27.6% repressed in both, with GO enrichment analysis. Peer reviewers accepted transcriptomic data without question as part of comprehensive gene expression analysis.

Both support protein-protein interaction reducing OsGLK1 transactivation (C99-C101). OpenEval details DLR assays showing OsNF-YB7 co-expression reduces OsGLK1-mediated activation. Peer reviewers accepted this functional consequence of dimerization as part of the interaction data demonstrating negative regulation.

Both support protein-protein interaction reducing DNA binding (C102-C103, C128-C130). OpenEval emphasizes EMSA showing reduced OsGLK1 binding with OsNF-YB7 present. Peer reviewers accepted this mechanism as part of the comprehensive demonstration of how OsNF-YB7-OsGLK1 interaction regulates downstream genes.

Both address comparison with Arabidopsis LEC1 (C2, C53, C135). OpenEval notes the contrast between osnf-yb7 increased chlorophyll and lec1 paler phenotype, acknowledging complexity in Arabidopsis literature. Peer reviewers affirmed the core finding without specifically addressing the Arabidopsis comparison nuances.

Both support rationale for focusing on OsGLK1 (C116-C117). OpenEval cites RNA-seq showing multiple TF upregulation and comprehensive characterization justifying OsGLK1 focus. Peer reviewers accepted the multi-layered regulatory model involving OsGLK1 without questioning the selection rationale.

Both address mechanistic speculation about OsNF-YB7 function (C125-C127). OpenEval supports C126 with DLR data while noting C127 is reasonable speculation. Peer reviewers accepted the direct binding and repression mechanism (C126) as rigorously validated without separately evaluating the speculative aspects.

Both support high-level summary of OsNF-YB7 as negative regulator (C36, C114). OpenEval synthesizes comprehensive experimental evidence. Peer reviewers explicitly affirmed this core conclusion, with all three reviewers emphasizing the convincing evidence for negative regulation of chlorophyll biosynthesis.

OpenEval evaluated background claims about chlorophyll biosynthesis and embryo development (C9-C13) as SUPPORTED literature review. Peer reviewers did not separately evaluate background/context claims, focusing instead on novel experimental findings.

OpenEval evaluated background claims about GLK genes (C14-C24) as SUPPORTED literature review providing context. Peer reviewers did not separately evaluate these established background claims, treating them as accepted context for the study.

OpenEval evaluated background claims about LEC1 (C25-C35) as SUPPORTED literature review. Peer reviewers did not separately evaluate these background claims, though the Arabidopsis comparison is implicit in their acceptance of the novel rice findings.

OpenEval evaluated discussion context about chlorophyllous embryos in plants (C104-C110) as SUPPORTED literature providing broader context. Peer reviewers did not separately evaluate these contextual claims from the discussion section.

OpenEval evaluated corroborating literature citations (C115, C132-C133) as SUPPORTED, noting independent validation and supporting evidence for post-translational GLK regulation. Peer reviewers did not separately evaluate these supporting citations from recent literature.

OpenEval rated reinterpretation of Arabidopsis LEC1 data (C134, C136-C141) as UNCERTAIN, noting the hypothesis challenges established views without new experimental data. Peer reviewers did not separately address this reinterpretation or the apparent contradiction with Arabidopsis literature.

OpenEval evaluated citation to previous work on OsNF-YB7's broader developmental roles (C142) as SUPPORTED context. Peer reviewers did not separately evaluate this contextual claim, though they accepted the genetic separation of chlorophyll from other developmental functions.

OpenEval evaluated established knowledge about GLK promoting chlorophyll biosynthesis (C5) as SUPPORTED by literature and validated by current study. Peer reviewers did not separately evaluate this foundational claim, treating it as accepted background.
